label: 灼烧子弹
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one full-bleed square 1:1 illustrated roguelike ability card reference, no typography and no card frame.
Input images: Image 1 is STYLE, established BLUE/IVORY player-mech palette and sunlit ruined battlefield reference only, not a composition to copy and not a reliable rear-body anatomy reference. Image 2 is the actual project Ground player mech front/upper-body and permanently side-mounted gun geometry; preserve its mechanical design, but use Image 1's blue/ivory paint instead of the model render's gold paint. Image 3 is the actual enemy Pioneer quadruped identity: rounded ivory armored hull, burgundy armor accents, four articulated legs, paired black side-mounted multi-barrel guns and two thin antennas. These are mechanical units, with no biological occupants visible.

Primary request: a single BURNING BULLET is the unmistakable hero of the picture. Use an extreme macro, racing-with-the-projectile perspective: the camera is ahead and slightly to one side of the oncoming round, looking back down its flight line. One sharp solid metal projectile, huge only because it is very close to the camera, occupies the central foreground on a dynamic diagonal. Its tapered pointed nose remains clearly readable through sculpted orange flame, a cream-hot core and a short fiery wake. Do not turn it into a missile, rocket, laser, orb or magical meteor.

Behind this bullet in the middle distance, an enemy Pioneer has just been punched through along that same firing line. Show a localized jagged torn opening in its armored hull, dark internal mechanical braces, outward-bent ivory and burgundy plates, scattered bolts, bent gun-mount pieces and fiery metal debris. Keep enough of its four-legged silhouette and paired side-gun design to identify the real unit. Mechanical destruction only, no gore.
Very close foreground fragments burn as they sweep past the frame edges. Draw elongated perspective speed streaks as a time-tunnel-like funnel that converges at a SINGLE distant vanishing point. This tunnel is created by velocity and streaks in a real battlefield, not a literal portal or science-fiction wormhole.
At that distant endpoint, show a small but identifiable blue-and-ivory Ground player mech firing its permanently attached right-side gun toward the viewer along the bullet's line. Its curved enclosed cockpit and upper-body geometry follow Image 2. The gun mount and torso are raised to aim; braced mechanical legs convey recoil. A small muzzle flash connects the source to the projectile's flight line. This mech has no human face, no neck, no palms or fingers, and no hand-held rifle.

Style: match Image 1's clean anime mechanical illustration, crisp varied dark outlines, matte large color blocks, three discrete cel-shaded lighting values, readable armor divisions, strong depth and kinetic framing. Fully painted opaque square background. Keep the bullet, the pierced Pioneer and the distant shooter in three distinct depth planes, with the bullet having the strongest contrast and detail. Retain recognizable ruined stone arches, sparse grass and sunlit sky only as simplified background anchors so they do not compete with the bullet.
Palette: existing blue/ivory mech and ivory/burgundy Pioneer identity; environmental families drawn from #6AA4BE, #274E61, #032E30, #557B78 and #D5C09C. Flame and warm light use #EE9D58 with #FEE4D9 highlights and restrained #8E3A2A hot edges. Derive cel-shadow shades from these colors. No photoreal textures, muddy gritty noise, excessive bloom or whiteout.
No text, letters, numbers, logo, watermark, borders, card frame, interface, diagrams, arrows, multiple panels, inset images or comparison sheet. Deliver ONE finished square illustration.

label: 灼烧爆裂子弹
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one full-bleed square 1:1 illustrated roguelike ability card reference, no typography and no card frame.
Input images: Image 1 supplies the established clean cel-shaded card illustration style, daylight ruined battlefield, grass and smoke treatment. Do not copy its composition or foreground player mech. Image 2 is the actual enemy Pioneer model and is the PRIMARY structural identity reference: an ivory rounded armored body with burgundy armor regions, FOUR articulated mechanical legs, two thin antennas and paired black side-mounted multi-barrel guns. Preserve that identity in the unbroken parts.

Primary request: depict a Pioneer erupting in a violent INTERNAL BURNING BURST. The main Pioneer fills the central picture in a dramatic three-quarter view, thrown off balance as a compact cream-hot and orange fire blast rips outward from inside its hull. The action must clearly read as an enemy mechanical unit exploding from within.
Its upper armor peels outward in several large readable ivory and burgundy pieces, revealing dark inner chassis bracing, sheared fasteners and localized electric sparks. One side-gun mounting is buckling from the blast. Keep the rounded hull, four-leg layout, antenna placement and side-gun arrangement recognizable, including clearly separated limbs rather than an amorphous pile of parts. Show a powerful blast at peak expansion without letting a giant fireball or smoke cloud hide the whole robot.

Supplement the user's core subject with a thin rapidly expanding shock ring close around the exploding unit, radial streaks and several flaming foreground armor fragments. Use a FEW large directional fragments instead of a cloud of confetti. Two smaller Pioneers farther to either side are visibly staggered by the expanding blast: raised legs, tilted hulls and local impact sparks, so the image communicates an area effect. They are secondary and remain less detailed and lower contrast than the central victim. No player mech is needed in the foreground.
Frame from a low dynamic camera, with a slightly tilted battlefield and strong near/far separation. The closest hot metal shards partially cross the picture edges. The shock ring is an energetic thin curved arc integrated into the scene, not a flat UI circle, targeting reticle, shield or magical rune.

Style: same clean anime mechanical card-art language as Image 1: crisp purposeful outlines, matte armor, clear three-tone cel shading, readable shape and silhouette, stylized evolving flame lobes and pale rose-gray smoke. Keep the sunlit grass and broken stone arches restrained in the distance. The blast has a cream-yellow hot core, warm orange edges, readable pale smoke, sparse sparks and strong radial action; avoid photorealism, muddy black smoke, overexposed white blobs, screen-filling fire, random dense panel noise and nuclear-mushroom imagery.
Palette: preserve Image 2's ivory and burgundy identity, using #FEE4D9, #A34053 and #662249 with dark #2C3735 mechanical interiors. Fire uses #EE9D58 and pale #FEE4D9 highlights; smoke may derive from #EABCBA and #835061. Contrast with cool #6AA4BE, #274E61 and #557B78 background families from the project palette.
Only machines and mechanical debris, no humans, blood or gore. No text, letters, numbers, logo, watermark, borders, card frame, interface, diagrams, arrows, multiple panels, inset images or comparison sheet. Deliver ONE finished square illustration.

label: 折射子弹正背面修正版
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: local anatomy correction to an existing full-bleed square illustrated roguelike card.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the current finished ricochet card. Image 2 is the actual Ground player mech viewed from the REAR three-quarter angle and is the authority for what belongs on its back. Image 3 is the same actual mech front/upper-body and permanently side-mounted weapon, provided only to distinguish front cockpit surfaces from rear exhaust and service panels. The gold model-render color is not the desired paint; retain the current card's blue, ivory and dark blue-gray paint.

Change ONLY the foreground player mech's mistaken front-versus-back body anatomy. In this camera, the player mech is seen from behind as it shoots toward the three enemies in the upper-right battlefield. Its forward-facing enclosed cockpit belongs on the far side, facing away toward those enemies. The large ivory chest/cockpit-like front plate currently presented to the viewer must instead become a coherent REAR body assembly matching Image 2: blue angular rear armor, dark recessed paired exhaust/service structures and warm horizontal slit details, with correctly connected back-to-waist supports. Rear components must read as machinery rather than eyes or a face. Do not leave front chest panels pasted onto its back and do not place a rear exhaust assembly on its front.
Maintain the same outer pose and apparent scale, the same torso lean, hip position, braced legs, blue-and-ivory identity and existing mechanical leg silhouette. Keep the gun on the mech's anatomical right side, fixed to its body, aimed along the current firing line toward the first enemy. Preserve the two bright attached lower-back exhaust plumes and their direction, correcting local attachment panels only if required to connect them mechanically.
The source model has an enclosed curved cockpit and no separate humanlike head, neck, hands, fingers or hand-held firearm. Reconcile the foreground surfaces with the actual rear design while retaining the illustration's style and existing blue paint.

Strict invariants: retain the original square canvas, camera, overall composition, tilted horizon, crop, lighting, color treatment, enemy count and placements. Preserve all THREE ivory-and-burgundy enemy Pioneers, their impact explosions and mechanical debris. Preserve the exact muzzle-to-first-enemy-to-second-to-third connected golden ricochet route with the same bend locations and directions. Preserve the sunlit ruined arches, grass, distant smoke, missiles, foreground rocks, dust and white speed lines. Do not mirror or flip the whole image or the whole mech; fix the mistaken body surfaces and rear layout by local redrawing. Outside the foreground mech and the small necessary connection edges, keep the target image unchanged.
Match the current crisp dark outlines, matte color blocks and three-tone anime cel shading. No recoloring the player to gold, no background restaging, no extra enemies, no new beams, no extra limbs, no whole-body rotation, no text, labels, watermark, UI or card frame. Deliver ONE corrected square illustration.
